Application Instructions
Apply Now
Welcome to the Office of Graduate Studies (OGS). Below you will find the application requirements for our PhD and Master’s programs in Biomedical Sciences. Please review all details carefully before beginning your application.
Online Application & Fees
+
–
Applications must be submitted via our application portal.
There is no fee to create an account and review the application. A non-refundable $85 processing fee is only due at the time of submission.
Transcripts & Academic Records
+
–
Standardized tests (GRE, GMAT) are not required.
Applicants must upload transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, including those from which a credential was not earned.
Unofficial transcripts, both domestic and international, are accepted at the time of application.
Unofficial transcripts must be submitted in PDF format.
However, if you are admitted to the program, you will be required to provide official transcripts via Parchment to the University of Miami - Graduate School before enrollment.
International transcripts that are not in English must be accompanied by an English translation.
International enrollees will be required to provide an external evaluation from a NACES member based on official documents that establish a U.S. Bachelor's degree equivalency before the issuance of an I-20 and enrollment.
English Proficiency
+
–
Applicants whose native language is not English must submit results from TOEFL, IELTS, or the Duolingo English Test (DET). Results from the TOEFL ibT Home Edition are acceptable but we do not accept TOEFL Essentials results. Test results must be less than two years old. Please refer to following for minimum acceptable test scores and waiver requirements: International Credentials & Applicants.
Official test results must be sent directly from the testing agency using the following codes:
TOEFL: Select University of Miami institutional code 5815.
IELTS: Select "University of Miami – Graduate School" from the options.
Duolingo: Select “University of Miami - Graduate School” from the options.
Due to changes in the TOEFL iBT scoring scale, the University of Miami Graduate School will require a minimum overall score of 4.5 for TOEFL iBT exams taken on or after January 21, 2026. Tests taken before this date will continue to use the past scoring scale.
English Language Test
Minimum Score*
TOEFL (iBT)
80 (before January 21, 2026)
4.5 (after January 21, 2026)
IELTS (Academic)
6.5
Duolingo English Test
125
Personal Statement
+
–
Applicants must submit a Personal Statement that describes their academic and research experiences, career goals, and motivations for pursuing a graduate degree at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine. Personal statements should not exceed three single spaced pages; most do not exceed two.
Resume/Curriculum Vitae
+
–
Some programs require applicants to submit a resume or CV that highlights the applicant’s research experience and relevant training. Experiences unrelated to science and scholarship should be omitted. Applicants that have published in peer reviewed journals of national or international reach should include the full citations, including PMID numbers if available. Applicants may include conference presentations and other scholarship in a separate section, but these must not be counted as peer reviewed publications elsewhere in your application. Resumes should not include headshots.
Letters of Recommendation
+
–
A minimum of three (and a maximum of five) letters of recommendation are required. Letters should come from individuals who are best able to assess your ability to be successful in a graduate program. For example, a research mentor or supervisor. Recommenders should provide a letter that is specific to the discipline for which you are applying.
Application Fee Waivers
+
–
Information about application fee waivers is available within our Application Portal. Please review the fee waiver section carefully when completing your application to ensure you are eligible before submitting a request.
Qualified applicants who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents may request a fee waiver based on financial need (e.g., falling below federal poverty guidelines) or participation in an approved program such as AmeriCorps or City Year, Fulbright Scholars, Gates Millennium Scholars, Peace Corps, or Teach for America.
Fee waivers are very limited and should be requested as early as possible.
If your fee waiver request is approved, you will receive an email notification from the program manager. Please do not contact the Office of Graduate Studies (OGS) Admissions regarding fee waiver status. Only applicants who are granted a waiver will be contacted.
Questions?
If you have any questions or need clarification, please contact the Office of Graduate by clicking the button below. We appreciate your interest in our programs and look forward to reviewing your application.
